descriptions: Basic infantry suited to capturing cities and defending forests.
Heavy armor for breakthroughs. Gains another attack after destroying a unit. +20% damage against infantry. Reduces small-arms damage by 72%. Receives armor kill rewards.
Range 2. Mobile siege artillery. The highest artillery class, delivering powerful direct fire.
Range 2. Deals 25% splash damage to nearby enemies and specializes in siege attacks. A counterattack has a 40% chance when attacking or being attacked.
Ignores terrain while moving. Can strike both fleets and ground forces.
A mainline naval vessel armed with anti-ship missiles and strong resistance to ground attacks. Range 3 against ground troops; anti-ship range 4.
Exclusive to Baekyang's capital. Stealth movement: +18 forest defense, 50% less counterattack damage, and ignores 30% of the target's defense.
Produced at airports. Ignores terrain and conducts powerful bombing attacks against ground forces and cities.
Grenade launcher. Range 1; deals 15% splash damage to nearby enemies.
Anti-tank rockets. Attack against armor is multiplied by 3.6. Counters tanks at short range.
Sustained fire. +60% damage against infantry.
Infantry squads with transport trucks, suited to rapid movement and capturing cities.
Wheeled armor that suppresses infantry with speed and repeated fire. +20% damage against infantry. Reduces small-arms damage by 50%. Receives armor kill rewards.
Fast armored reconnaissance and breakthroughs. Gains another attack after a kill. +20% damage against infantry. Reduces small-arms damage by 65%. Receives armor kill rewards.
Elite heavy tank with range 2 and strong armor. Gains another attack after a kill. +20% damage against infantry. Reduces small-arms damage by 78%. Receives armor kill rewards.
Light indirect-fire weapon. Range 1, providing inexpensive siege support.
Heavy towed field gun. Range 2, with increased damage when bombarding cities.

Exclusive to Dante's capital. Hell Charge: +25% on the first attack after moving, and consecutive attacks after kills. A demonic mount with reinforced armor. Reduces small-arms damage by 60%. Its staff fires a red laser at range 3. +20% damage against infantry.
Range 2. Exclusive to Stetopia's capital. Robotic steed with laser artillery: ignores 50% of enemy defense and deals 20% damage to nearby enemies.
Produced at level-5 airport cities. Conducts long-range area bombing and nuclear delivery missions.
Mobile support aircraft. Flies over land and sea and attacks with an autocannon. Cannot capture cities and is affected by anti-air defenses.
Heavily armed helicopter with anti-tank missiles. +80% damage against armor. Flies over land and sea but cannot capture cities.
Fast coastal vessel with repeated cannon fire. Range 3 against ground troops; anti-ship range 3.
Armed with anti-ship missiles and escort defenses. Protects friendly transports within 9 tiles against conventional bombing and ballistic missiles. Range 3 against ground troops; anti-ship range 4.
Heavily armored destroyer. Powerful anti-ship missiles inflict heavy damage on transports. Range 3 against ground troops; anti-ship range 5.

Exclusive to level-5 harbor cities of Baekyang, Dante and Stetopia. Carrier aircraft conduct bombing missions. Up to 5 attacks per turn, consuming 2 oil per attack. Deals 20 times its attack value against cities.
Carries up to 20 units. Takes no conventional bombing or ballistic missile damage within 9 tiles of a friendly frigate. Vulnerable to anti-ship missiles. All embarked units are lost if it sinks.

stories.0: Riflemen are the heart of the battle. Even on streets swept by shells, their hands make the final knock on the door. Back home, people still wait for family who have not returned.
stories.1: A tank is a fighting machine with formidable firepower and armor. Inside the steel hull, its crew repeat their duties among shells, instruments and radios.
stories.2: Self-propelled artillery carries a heavy gun into position. A fire order fills the cramped compartment with movement. To a loader, the weight of a shell means more than a number.
stories.3: Multiple rocket launchers strike an area with successive rockets. After firing, their empty tubes must be filled again. Supply vehicles approach through lingering smoke.
stories.4: Fighters approach their targets swiftly from the sky. Before takeoff, the pilot adjusts their gloves while the mechanics finish their checks. At the end of the runway, they exchange the same familiar wave.
stories.5: Engine-room sailors recognize a colleague by their footsteps before their voice. The same kettle passes between watches, and nobody replaces the worn cloth around its handle. Even the oldest engineer cannot remember who first wrapped it.
stories.7: Bombers carry heavy loads toward distant targets. In flight, the crew count the hours while checking instruments and their route. After returning, they count people before inspecting the aircraft.
stories.8: Grenadiers fight enemies behind walls and cover. Squadmates joke about their heavy ammunition pouches, but look for them first when combat begins.
stories.9: Anti-tank infantry are small teams facing enormous steel vehicles. They share the weight of their equipment and wait in the mud for a chance to fire a single rocket.
stories.10: Heavy machine gunners fill a crossing with fire. The assistant feeding the long belt and the gunner cooling the barrel know each other's rhythm. When the firing stops, they reach for water first.
stories.11: For motorized infantry, the truck is both transport and temporary lodging. Ammunition, gold and silently sleeping soldiers share its dust-covered cargo bed.
stories.12: Armored cars cross the front with speed and repeated fire. To the crew, the cramped interior is both workplace and living space. The engine always makes conversation a shouting match.
stories.13: Light tanks open the way with speed and maneuver. Relying on quick decisions rather than thick armor, their crews study even the smallest contours on a map.
stories.14: Elite tanks undertake the fiercest breakthroughs. Their experienced crews, handling heavy armor and powerful guns, notice every unusual sound. Only after maintenance do they begin their late meal.
stories.15: Mortars provide indirect fire close to the infantry. For crews carrying short barrels and heavy rounds, each day begins and ends with dismantling and assembly.
stories.16: Towed guns are an old instrument for striking distant targets. The gunners pulling them, digging positions and carrying ammunition always have dirt and oil on their clothes.
stories.19: Strategic bombers carry heavy loads along long routes. Before flight, their crews repeatedly check the course and fuel. Maintenance lights remain on in the hangar late into the night.
stories.20: Light attack helicopters skim the low skies of the front. The pilot reads the terrain while the gunner talks to ground troops. Returning aircraft are met by waiting mechanics.
stories.21: Attack helicopters track tanks and wait for a clear firing opportunity. Their two crew members alternate between instruments and targets. After the mission, ammunition and fuel must be replenished.
stories.22: A dry pair of socks is an unexpected luxury aboard a fast attack craft. When a newcomer spills coffee on deck, the veterans check their shoes before the cup. The last question before sailing is usually who brought snacks.
stories.23: The frigate's mess has a table with one short leg. The crew believe that removing the playing card beneath it will spill the next meal's soup. Any game needing that card always remains unfinished at sea.
stories.24: A destroyer's corridors look remarkably alike to a newcomer. Veteran sailors navigate by peeling paint and the hum of ventilation. Anyone caught pretending to know the way finds a hand-drawn map on their bunk the next day.
stories.25: The carrier's night bakery is surprisingly popular. When fresh bread drifts up the vents, sailors from different watches meet on the same stairway. The cook insists that disappearing loaves reveal shift changes more accurately than the ship's clock.
stories.26: Soldiers boarding a transport first seek a window seat, then a place that rolls less. Bags from different units become mixed, and disembarkation begins with disputes over borrowed blankets. The crew remember the most seasick passenger more readily than the highest-ranking officer.
